title: Smoky Chicken Enchiladas
subtitle: From scratch · no kit needed · serves 6
description: Chicken thigh, peppers and onions in a homemade smoky-barbecue fajita seasoning, bound in a passata-based enchilada sauce, rolled into tortillas and baked under cheese. Everything the Old El Paso box gives you, made from cupboard spices.

steps.text: Warm the {{sauce-oil}} in a saucepan over medium heat and stir in the {{sauce-cumin}}, {{sauce-paprika}}, {{sauce-smoked-paprika}}, {{sauce-chilli}}, {{sauce-garlic}}, {{sauce-onion}}, {{sauce-oregano}} and {{sauce-cloves}}. Cook until fragrant, then pour in the {{passata}}, {{tomato-puree}}, {{sauce-water}}, {{sauce-sugar}} and {{sauce-salt}}.

Simmer gently to develop the flavour. Mix the {{sauce-cornflour}} with a splash of cold water, stir it in and cook until glossy. Blitz smooth with a stick blender if you like, then set the sauce aside.

In a small bowl, stir together the {{faj-smoked-paprika}}, {{faj-paprika}}, {{faj-cumin}}, {{faj-garlic}}, {{faj-onion}}, {{faj-sugar}}, {{faj-salt}}, {{faj-cornflour}}, {{faj-chilli}}, {{faj-oregano}} and {{faj-pepper}} to make the smoky fajita seasoning.
Heat the oven to 200°C / 180°C fan. Fry the {{chicken}} in a little {{oil}} over high heat until sealed all over, then cook 1 minute more.
Add the {{onion}} and {{pepper}} and cook until soft and lightly charred at the edges.
Scatter in the fajita seasoning and stir for a minute or two until everything is coated and aromatic.
Stir in HALF the enchilada sauce and half the {{cheddar}} to make a thick filling. Keep the other half of the sauce and cheese back for the top.
Spoon the filling down the middle of each {{wraps}}, roll up, and lay them seam-side down in a baking dish.
Spoon over the reserved sauce to cover, then scatter with the reserved cheese.
Bake until the sauce is bubbling and the cheese is golden. Rest a couple of minutes before serving.

notes: Makes 12 enchiladas — two per person for six.
The sauce and seasoning here are homemade stand-ins for the two Old El Paso kit sachets. Both scale with the servings, so you always make the right amount.
Heat is mild like the kit. For medium, add a pinch of cayenne to the seasoning or bump the sauce chilli.
Good with soured cream, guacamole and rice on the side.
The smoky-barbecue note comes from the smoked paprika plus brown sugar in the seasoning — a little grated dark chocolate or ½ tsp cocoa in the sauce deepens it further if you want.

nutrition.note: Rough estimate for the recipe as written, per person (two enchiladas). Actual values depend on your wraps, cheese and cut of chicken.
